svg.title: RIEMANN · MAP R3 — From prime sums to the zero-free half-plane: the analytic half of the proof, lemma by lemma
svg.desc: The chapter proves one theorem: if families of definite unitary groups carry slope data, and auxiliary CM fields exist at every scale of long windows, then no primitive Dirichlet L-function vanishes right of the critical line. Its blueprint chapter has five sections and 24 statements, and every one is a card here: the Lean declaration, the statement, the proof and what it uses. Read it from the foot up: the theorem is at the bottom, its two inputs stand on either side, and each column above is one strand of the argument. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that B takes A as a hypothesis, which the proof text names and the uses list does not. The blueprint says of this chapter that the square root in the core inequality is the Riemann Hypothesis. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5. Map mode: nothing of the blueprint's text or the proof's source is quoted.

svg.text: Top row: the five definitions the chapter is written in. Left column: Landau's theorem, then the auxiliary fields. Second column: the core inequality. The top row of results and the right half: the local link at inert primes, from a mean value theorem for bad shares up to the lattice-gain bound, and slope data from it. Nothing is used before it is proved.

thm-zero-free-from-connected is stated with two hypotheses: that families have slope
data (def-connected-families), and that auxiliary CM fields with the properties of
thm-auxiliary-fields exist at the scales of long windows.
Its proof says that hypothesis 1 comes from thm-families-connected and hypothesis 2
from thm-auxiliary-fields, and proves neither: the Lean theorem takes them as
arguments. The blueprint's uses list for the proof names neither, so no solid arrow joins them.
The dashed arrows are the diagram's reading of that sentence. The theorem that discharges
both hypotheses is thm-zero-free-from-families in the outline chapter (diagram R1,
